name: Amiodarone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

key_interactions.drug_or_class: QT-prolonging drugs (class I and III antiarrhythmics, lithium, some phenothiazines, tricyclics, some fluoroquinolones and macrolides, azole antifungals)
key_interactions.effect: Higher risk of torsade de pointes (label).
Serious symptomatic bradycardia, some needing pacemakers, one fatal (label).
key_interactions.action: Monitor heart rate if starting antivirals in patients taking or recently stopping amiodarone.

key_interactions.effect: INR rises about 100% within 3 to 4 days; serious or fatal bleeding (label).
key_interactions.action: Reduce the warfarin dose by one-third to one-half and monitor INR closely.
Halve or stop digoxin; if continued, monitor levels closely.
Limit simvastatin to 20 mg and lovastatin to 40 mg daily; lower doses of other CYP3A4 statins may be needed.

key_interactions.effect: Persistently high cyclosporine levels with rising creatinine (label).
key_interactions.action: Monitor cyclosporine levels and kidney function.

key_interactions.drug_or_class: Beta-blockers, verapamil, diltiazem, digoxin, ivabradine, clonidine
key_interactions.effect: Bradycardia, sinus arrest and AV block (label).

key_interactions.action: Start them at lower doses; reduce existing doses by 30 to 50% after adding oral amiodarone.

key_interactions.effect: Cimetidine raises and cholestyramine lowers amiodarone levels (label).
